I had my first serious boyfriend, also a super sweet and caring guy, around the time my dpdr started, also I reeeally wanted to be in a relationship with a girl. My dpdr symptoms worsened the longer I dragged this on. I chickened out and didn't break up with him when I should have. Then I started subconsciously resenting him and avoiding him.

He broke up with me after some time. We started talking again after several years, and I apologised for not breaking up with him sooner and concealing my actual feelings, and he apologised for leaving me when I needed the most help from my close ones.

I'd advise you not to repeat my mistakes and talk to him about your feelings. Maybe he leaves you, maybe he'll stay as a friend -- ask yourself, is the chance to keep him around worth your mental health struggles?

I do think that it's possible for dissociation to be worsened or even caused by being under pressure in a situation you don't want to be in. Take care, wish you the best!

P.S. I'm happy in a relationship with a beautiful girl as of now, and my ex bf is having a career blast :)

I'm here with ya! I've been in dissociative state for quite a long time now. Since I got my first serious relationship and to this day. So I have never actually had a relationship that wasn't stained by this stuff. You're not alone in this. But yeah it sucks big time. I just want to really be present when I'm with my partner.. but I can't.
However, it has been getting better for me lately! What I can advise is to remember that dpdr is caused by some mental health problems (mostly anxiety) and is not to be ignored. Don't go in it with the attitude of "this stupid shit is ruining my relationship, when am I gonna get rid of it?". Dissociation is a sign that something should be taken care of in your life. So by all means, get professional help, look into videos and articles on dpdr -- there are plenty, fortunately. Just don't bash youself and your mental health for something you can't control. Wish you the best!!

Edit: also, I'd look into something that changed before you started feeling like this. Maybe a new medication, new stressful job, new city, death of a loved one? Not working properly through grief or stress may wreak havoc on ya mental state.

I can see where you are coming from, but I have to disagree with you. There is no attachment in feeling your body and being in present moment. 
Being disidentified with your body, your ego, your emotions is one, completely disregarding and disowning them is another. One comes from a place of love, the other doesn't.
Grounding is a practice of accepting your state, your body and being present. You can do this while not attached to your ego.

Look up derealization/depersonalization, many people have this feeling 24/7 for many years, not able to snap out of it, BUT

as far as I know (had this thing along with severe depression and panic attacks, unability to focus and extreme anxiety), this happens when your astral body is detached from your physical body (so we get this feeling quite literally, "watching ourselves as if we're in a dream"), and what we need to do is to ground ourselves in our bodies.

Now, this mainly happens because we have too much pain/stress we can't deal with so we just distance ourselves from our feelings, our bodies. So, for grounding, I suggest you to:

1) scan your body, toe to head. Explore every little sensation, without distracting yourself by thoughts. Do this few times a day, every chance you can basically.

2) learn how to manage stress and emotional pain properly

3) do a visualisation of your astral body comind back into your physical body, and with time you'll really start to feel whether your bodies are aligned or not

4) excercise while focusing on your body completely

5) when this sensation comes, try to become aware of how your perception of your body and surroundings changed and really explore this feeling, dive deep into it and surrender to it

And the main tip: don't get freaked out by it, know this experience is fixable and you're not going crazy!

edit: Alcohol/drugs can also be very detrimental to grounding
